newsitem.title: POLAND: Cash-short market to keep Polish T-bill yields up.
newsitem.headline: Cash-short market to keep Polish T-bill yields up.

text.p: The cash-short Polish money market, strapped for funds after repeated long-term central bank drainages, is likely to limit demand at Monday's primary T-bill tender and underpin yields, analysts said on Friday.
They expected demand to fall from this week's 1.98 billion but still to double the treasury's 600 million zloty offer.
"If the money market situation remains the same, I expect yields to hold flat or inch up at Monday's tender," said Piotr Korcz, T-bill dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.

Analysts expected the benchmark 52-week T-bill yield to hold flat at 19.42 percent or inch up toward secondary market levels of 19.50 percent and the 26-week paper to remain at the 19.11 percent level from the previous tender.
They said, however, that bill-hungry non-banking sector clients would likely keep a lid on 13-week yields, last at 18.60 percent and could even knock them slightly down.
"The shortest 13-week treasuries are most popular with firms and next week's offer is quite small," said Piotr Bednarek, head T-bill dealer at ING bank in Warsaw.
On Monday the treasury will offer 400 million zlotys of 52-week T-bills and 100 million of each 26- and 13-week paper.

Analysts said the National Bank of Poland's recent drainages, using mainly longer-term NBP-bills and not 14-day reverse repos in line with its policy to lenghten banks' cash-flow horizons, kept the market short-of cash this week.
"Many banks probably over-invested in high-yielding NPB-bills and are now searching for one-day cash to cover daily needs," said one foreign bank dealer in Warsaw.
The central bank sold in September 2.72 billion zlotys of NBP-bills, maturing in 91-, 182- and 273-days.
"Liquidity is not likely to return to the market from Monday, but rates may normalise late in the week as cash returns," said Renata Krajewska, dealer at PKO BP.
Overnight and tomorrow/next rates closed at the week around discount rate levels of 22 percent, up from the market's main 14-day drainage rate at 19.15 percent.

Analysts were mixed on whether the zloty would continue to hold in its weeks-old band between 1.9 and 1.5 percent from the central pority rate, or edge lower under pressure from importer bids and delicate foreign withdrawal from Polish T-bills. @
"Much depends on foreign investor activity next week, but we could see the zloty begin drift down in the direction of 1.2 percent from parity," said Bogdan Stepkowski of ING.
The zloty closed the week at 2.7850 to the dollar and 1.8410 to the mark, about 1.71 percent from the parity rate.
